source_refs.note: Topic 23.7 (PDF 112-113). The book says the boiling point of ethyl ethanoate shows its 'lower relative volatility'; a lower boiling point means higher volatility, as the lesson says. A repeated sentence is not duplicated; the fruit photographs are not reproduced.

blocks.text: Esters are derivatives of carboxylic acids formed by their reaction with alcohols. Unlike alcohols and carboxylic acids, esters cannot form hydrogen bonds between their own molecules, so their boiling points are lower than those of the corresponding alcohols and carboxylic acids: ethyl ethanoate, CH3COOC2H5, boils at 77 C, showing that it is more volatile than ethanoic acid and ethanol. The lack of hydrogen bonding also makes esters less soluble in water. Many esters are liquids with sweet, fruity smells, and they are used as solvents and as flavourings in fruit drinks and sweets; the fragrance and taste of many fruits are due to esters.
